transit:1.sentence: carries as many subway riders a year as Mexico City
transit:1.note: MTA 2025 subway ridership; Mexico City Metro's 2025 ridership, the agency's own year-end figure as reported by the Quadratin news agency (the agency's site was not reachable). Both count entries rather than journeys, so they are measured the same way. Mexico City's metro is the second busiest in the Americas after New York's.

transit:8.sentence: logs as many bike-share rides a year as Paris does on Vélib'
transit:8.caveat: Paris's figure is a year behind.
transit:8.note: Lyft's March 2026 post on Citi Bike operations ('more than 46 million rides in 2025'); Vélib' trips in 2024 as reported by the French cycling trade site Cleanrider, because velib-metropole.fr blocks automated fetching. Vélib' is the older and larger-docked system; Citi Bike has more bikes.

transit:4.sentence: draws as many visitors a year as all of Turkey
transit:4.caveat: Turkey's count includes Turkish citizens living abroad who come to visit.
transit:4.note: New York City Tourism + Conventions annual report for 2025; the Turkish Statistical Institute's 2025 total visitor figure as reported by Daily Sabah. Turkey was the world's fourth most visited country. France's population (68.6 million) was the earlier comparison here.

land:9.sentence: has as many street trees as Toronto
land:9.caveat: New York City's count is from 2015-16; a new census is under way.
land:9.note: NYC Parks TreesCount 2015-2016; Toronto's street-tree inventory as compiled by the University of Toronto's School of Cities, because Toronto's own open-data page was retired. Both count municipally owned street trees and exclude park trees. Toronto has a third of New York City's population.

wealth:1.sentence: has as many jobs as the whole Chicago metropolitan area
wealth:1.caveat: Chicago's figure covers a three-state metropolitan area; New York City's covers the five boroughs.
wealth:1.note: Total nonfarm payroll jobs, July 2026, not seasonally adjusted, from the Bureau of Labor Statistics series for New York City and for the Chicago-Naperville-Elgin metropolitan area, both as published on FRED. Kuwait's population (4.90 million) was the earlier comparison here.

health:1.sentence: has as many people on food stamps as all of Illinois
health:1.caveat: Illinois's figure is four months earlier. Caseloads are falling in both places.
health:1.note: Human Resources Administration HRA Facts for July 2026; Illinois participation in March 2026 from the U.S. Department of Agriculture's state SNAP tables. Phoenix's population (1.67 million) was the earlier comparison here.

people:2.sentence: has as many foreign-born residents as Los Angeles County
people:2.caveat: Los Angeles County holds 9.8 million people to New York City's 8.5 million.
people:2.note: Both figures are the same Census Bureau table and year: American Community Survey 2024 one-year estimates, table B05002, variable B05002_013E ('Foreign-born'), queried for New York city and for Los Angeles County. This also confirms the City Planning Department's rounded 3.1 million. Armenia's population (3.10 million) was the earlier comparison here.

people:12.sentence: has as many residents 65 and older as Los Angeles County
people:12.note: Both figures are the same Census Bureau table and year: American Community Survey 2024 one-year estimates, subject table S0101, variable S0101_C01_030E ('65 years and over'), queried for New York city and for Los Angeles County. This is more current than the State Comptroller's 1.43 million for 2023, which the earlier version of this line used against Estonia's population.

people:11.sentence: had as many marathon finishers in 2025 as London
people:11.note: New York Road Runners' count for the Nov. 2, 2025 race, as reported by Running USA; London Marathon Events' own announcement for its April 2025 race. London set the world record for the largest marathon in April and New York took it back in November. Anfield's capacity was the earlier comparison here.

people:3.sentence: has as many students in its district schools as Colorado has in all its public schools
people:3.caveat: Counting the city's roughly 150,000 charter pupils and its pre-K would put New York City ahead of Colorado rather than behind it.
people:3.note: Department of Education preliminary 2025-26 K-12 district enrollment, as reported by City Journal quoting the department; Colorado Department of Education's 2025-26 enrollment release. Counting New York City's charter schools and pre-K would put the city well above Colorado. North Dakota's population (799,358) was the earlier comparison here.

learning:5.sentence: sold as many Yankees tickets in 2025 as the Phillies sold in Philadelphia
learning:5.note: Both clubs' 2025 home attendance from the same ESPN season table, so the methodology matches. The Mets drew 3,182,052. Uruguay's population (3.39 million) was the earlier comparison here.

land:8.sentence: has as much parkland as El Paso
land:8.note: Both figures come from the Trust for Public Land's 2026 ParkScore index, which applies one definition of parkland to the 100 largest U.S. cities, so the two sides are measured identically. NYC Parks' own figure is 'more than 30,000 acres'. San Antonio (28,830 acres) was the next closest; San Diego, Houston, Los Angeles and Phoenix all have far more. The island of Jersey was the earlier comparison here.

money:10.sentence: has real estate worth as much as Mexico produces in a year
money:10.caveat: Department of Finance market values are the city's own estimates and lag sale prices.
money:10.note: Total market value of all city property on the fiscal 2027 tentative assessment roll, published Jan. 15, 2026; the International Monetary Fund's 2025 estimate of Mexico's nominal GDP. Spain's 2024 GDP was the earlier comparison, but the year gap was two years and its 2025 estimate is too high.

people:10.sentence: shelters as many homeless people each night as Andorra has people
people:10.caveat: Department of Homeless Services shelters only; other agencies' shelters and migrant sites are not included.
people:10.note: Department of Homeless Services daily report dated Sept. 2, 2026; the PDF at that address is overwritten every day, so the figure cannot be re-read there later. Andorra's population is the World Bank's 2025 figure, verified live. Sources disagree on Andorra: its own Department of Statistics was reported as giving 89,058 registered residents at the end of 2025, about 7 percent higher, and its site is a JavaScript portal that could not be read to confirm. The World Bank series is used because it was checked directly and is the same series behind the other population comparisons on this page.

land:5.sentence: has as many miles of sewer as the Earth is wide
land:5.note: The Environmental Protection Department's 'in-city sewers' figure, against Earth's equatorial diameter as given by NASA. The department's sewer-system page separately says 'over 7,400 miles'.

land:11.sentence: has as many fire hydrants as London
land:11.caveat: London's hydrants are split across four water companies; New York City's belong to one utility. Both figures are rounded.
land:11.note: The Environmental Protection Department's own figure, against the London Fire Brigade's count of the hydrants it inspects. This replaces a comparison with Aruba's population. Berlin (69,300), Los Angeles (about 61,000) and Chicago (about 47,000) were all far too small.

transit:3.sentence: gives as many bus rides a year as the European Union has people
transit:3.caveat: New York City Transit buses only; the MTA Bus Company adds about 120 million.
transit:3.note: MTA 2025 bus ridership for New York City Transit; the World Bank's 2025 population for the European Union, the most recent on that series.

crime:7.sentence: makes as many arrests a year as Buffalo has people
crime:7.note: Row count of 2025 arrests in the NYPD Arrests Data (Historic) dataset on NYC Open Data, all ages; Buffalo's population in the Census Bureau's own Vintage 2025 file. An earlier version used a third-party aggregator's Vintage 2024 figure of 276,854; the Bureau's newer estimate has Buffalo shrinking.

crime:6.sentence: answers as many 911 calls a year as all of North Carolina
crime:6.caveat: New York City's is a fiscal year to June 2025; North Carolina's is calendar 2025.
crime:6.note: NYPD 911 calls in fiscal 2025 from the Mayor's Management Report, against calls answered by every emergency call centre in North Carolina, from the state's 911 Board. This replaces a comparison with Arizona's population.

crime:3.sentence: sends an ambulance as many times a year as Philadelphia has people
crime:3.note: FDNY emergency medical incidents in fiscal 2025 from the Mayor's Management Report; Philadelphia's population in the Census Bureau's Vintage 2025 estimates.

wealth:0.sentence: has as many millionaires as the Bay Area
wealth:0.caveat: The Bay Area here is San Francisco plus Silicon Valley, a region rather than a city. Both counts mean at least $1 million in liquid, investable assets.
wealth:0.note: Both figures come from the same Henley & Partners World's Wealthiest Cities Report for 2025, so the methodology matches on both sides. This replaces a comparison with the population of the Bahamas. The same report notes the Bay Area now has more billionaires than New York City, 82 against 66.

wealth:7.sentence: has a Staten Island whose economy is the size of Mongolia's
wealth:7.caveat: Both figures are 2024. The IMF puts Mongolia 7 percent higher in 2025.
wealth:7.note: Bureau of Economic Analysis 2024 GDP for Richmond County via FRED; the IMF's figure for Mongolia's 2024 nominal GDP. This line previously used Guyana, whose oil-driven economy the IMF already puts 14 percent higher for 2025, which made the pairing stale on the day it was published.

people:6.sentence: has as many people on the city payroll as Texas has state employees
people:6.caveat: Both are actual full-time headcounts. The federal survey reflects a March 2025 payroll.
people:6.note: Actual full-time employees in April 2026 from the city Comptroller, against full-time state government employment for Texas in the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of Public Employment and Payroll. This replaces a comparison with Pittsburgh's population. New York State's own government, at 238,904, is 18 percent smaller than the city payroll.

wealth:4.sentence: has as many Wall Street jobs as Alphabet has employees worldwide
wealth:4.caveat: New York City's figure is preliminary.
wealth:4.note: State Comptroller's March 2026 report on securities-industry employment in 2025 (preliminary; the 2024 figure was a 30-year high of 201,500), against Alphabet's employee count at Dec. 31, 2025 from its Form 10-K. Both sides are now 2025: an earlier version of this line paired 2024 employment against Alphabet's end-2025 headcount.

likeforlike:17.sentence: has as many miles of water main as Los Angeles
likeforlike:17.note: Mains against mains. The Environmental Protection Department maintains 'over 6,800 miles of in-city water mains'; the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power's 2024-25 infrastructure plan reports 'approximately 6,794 miles of Mainline Pipe' as a separate category from its 547 miles of larger trunk line and its 300-mile aqueduct. An earlier version of this line compared New York City's mains against Los Angeles's mains and trunk lines combined, 7,341 miles, which was not the same category.

people:9.sentence: employs as many public school teachers as all of Ireland
people:9.caveat: Ireland counts allocated posts, which are full-time equivalents; New York City's is a headcount, so the two are not exactly the same unit.
people:9.note: Mayor's Management Report, fiscal 2025, against the Irish Department of Education's July 2025 education indicators for the 2023/24 school year. An earlier version of this line used Ireland's 2022 figure of 74,073, which an audit flagged as four years stale, and carried a caveat saying Ireland had probably overtaken New York City since. A later check found that claim unsupported, because the city's own teacher count has been rising too: a February 2026 city report puts New York City schools at about 81,000 teachers as of October 2025. Both sides are growing, and on the figures each publishes they remain close.

health:0.sentence: has as many people on Medicaid as all of Florida
health:0.caveat: New York City's month is July 2026, Florida's April 2026.
health:0.note: New York State Department of Health enrollment by residential county, July 2026, against Florida's total Medicaid and CHIP enrollment as tabulated by KFF from federal data. This replaces a comparison with Utah's population. Both sides now count people enrolled in Medicaid.

health:7.sentence: has as many residents with a disability as Virginia
health:7.caveat: Civilian, non-institutional population on both sides.
health:7.note: Both figures come from the same Census Bureau table, variable and year: American Community Survey 2024 one-year estimates, subject table S1810, queried for New York city and for every state. This replaces a comparison with Montana's population. Washington (1,083,349) and Tennessee (1,058,522) were the next closest.

learning:1.sentence: has as many college students as all of Massachusetts
learning:1.caveat: Massachusetts is fall 2022, the latest year in the federal table; New York City's is a 2024 count.
learning:1.note: New York City Economic Development Corporation's November 2024 report on academia, against total fall enrollment in degree-granting institutions in Massachusetts from the federal Digest of Education Statistics. This replaces a comparison with Cabo Verde's population. Massachusetts's own 2017 enrollment was 503,539, almost exactly New York City's figure today.

transit:6.sentence: is served by airports that carry as many passengers as Istanbul's
transit:6.caveat: Newark is in New Jersey and Stewart is in Orange County, so this is the regional airport system rather than airports inside the city.
transit:6.note: The Port Authority's own 2025 annual traffic report, replacing a news account of it, against Istanbul's two airports as reported by Hurriyet Daily News. Both are multi-airport city systems run by more than one operator. This replaces a comparison with Russia's population. London's five airports (178.2 million) and Paris's two (107.0 million) were both too far off.

learning:4.sentence: draws as many museum visitors to the Met as the Uffizi draws in Florence
learning:4.caveat: Both are multi-site museums: the Met counts Fifth Avenue and the Cloisters, the Uffizi counts the gallery, the Pitti Palace and the Boboli Gardens.
learning:4.note: The Met's fiscal 2025 attendance from its own announcement, against the Uffizi's calendar 2025 attendance in The Art Newspaper's annual survey of museum visitor figures. This replaces a comparison with Finland's population. The British Museum, at 6.5 million, was 14 percent off.

learning:7.sentence: fills as many Broadway seats at home as touring Broadway fills everywhere else
learning:7.note: Both figures are the Broadway League's own, for the same 2024-25 season: 14.7 million attendances in New York City's theatres against 14.9 million across the North American touring circuit. This replaces a comparison with Guinea's population. London's West End drew 17.1 million in calendar 2024, 16 percent more, which was too far off and a different reporting period.
